title: AlphaNIST: Emergent Assembly Skills from Binary Task Rewards
abstract: arXiv:2610.13354v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The NIST Assembly Task Board #1 remains a challenging benchmark for learning-based methods in robotic manipulation. Over short horizons, it demands precise, contact-rich control of small, tight-fitting parts. Over long horizons, it requires recovery and coordination across extended action sequences. Demonstrations, task decomposition, and dense progress rewards have enabled research advances by providing guidance on how to assemble. But how much of the strategy must be specified? The progression from AlphaGo to AlphaGo Zero showed that RL at scale can discover superhuman strategies without prescribing how to win. AlphaNIST asks whether a sparse binary task reward and task diversity admitted by this task-agnostic reward can similarly let a robot discover how to assemble. In simulation, we train a single policy from scratch across all 20 assembly tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board #1, reaching 98.2% overall training success without demo

translated_title: AlphaNIST：从二元任务奖励中涌现的装配技能
translated_abstract: NIST装配任务板1号（NIST Assembly Task Board #1）仍然是机器人操作领域基于学习方法的一个具有挑战性的基准。在短时间尺度上，它要求对小型、紧密配合的零件进行精确且富含接触的控制；在长时间尺度上，它需要在延长的动作序列中进行恢复与协调。演示数据、任务分解和密集的进度奖励通过提供“如何装配”的指导推动了研究进展。但是，策略中究竟有多少必须被显式规定？从AlphaGo到AlphaGo Zero的演进表明，大规模强化学习可以在不规定如何获胜的情况下发现超越人类的策略。AlphaNIST探究的是：稀疏的二元任务奖励，以及这种任务无关奖励所能容纳的任务多样性，是否同样能让机器人自行发现如何进行装配。在仿真中，我们从零开始训练一个单一策略，涵盖NIST装配任务板1号上的全部20个装配任务，在无演示的情况下达到了98.2%的总体训练成功率。
tldr: 受AlphaGo Zero启发，该研究仅用稀疏的二元任务奖励从零开始训练单一策略，在仿真中无需演示或密集奖励即可完成NIST装配任务板1号全部20个装配任务，达到98.2%的训练成功率。
en_tdlr: Inspired by AlphaGo Zero, AlphaNIST trains a single policy from scratch using only sparse binary task rewards, achieving 98.2% training success across all 20 assembly tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board #1 without demonstrations or dense reward shaping.
